metadata.case_name: LI YUK CHING v. SECRETARY FOR JUSTICE

plaintiff.occupation_before: Cultural Services Assistant II in the Arts Museum
plaintiff.occupation_after: Transferred to the Chang Sha Wan Abattoir (on or about 1993-10-25)

injuries.description: The neck was showing the typical course of a flexion injury - extreme discomfort and pain, and restriction of movement with remissions and relapses requiring courses of physiotherapy and perhaps traction and manipulation from time to time.
source: The neck was showing the typical course of a flexion injury - extreme discomfort and pain, and restriction of movement with remissions and relapses requiring courses of physiotherapy and perhaps traction and manipulation from time to time.
there was marked loss of lordosis (inward curve of the spine) and she now had cervical kyphosis (outward curve of the spine) which was likely to give rise to cervical spondylosis
injuries.icd_description: Acute whiplash associated disorder with complaint of neck pain with musculoskeletal signs

injuries.description: Disc prolapse at C6-7 level disclosed on MRI.
source: In November 1996 an M.R.I. Scan was performed and disclosed a disc prolapse at C6-7 level.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the neck

injuries.description: Partial nerve palsy of the left index finger consequent upon nerve injury to the neck.
source: she had mild residual neck pain and a partial nerve palsy of her left index finger consequent upon the nerve injury to her neck which was now (3 years later) unlikely to recover.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of peripheral nerves of neck

injuries.description: Left shoulder was struck and pinioned by or in the hydraulic bracket; head forced against and struck the counter.
source: the consequence of the door closing on the Plaintiff, an ever present risk, was that her left shoulder was struck and pinioned by or in the hydraulic bracket and her head was forced against and struck the counter.
injuries.icd_description: Crushing injury of shoulder or upper arm

injuries.description: Emergence of lumbar pain (back pain extending from T12 level to L3) first complained of in or about September 1996.
injuries.body_part: lower back / lumbar region (T12 to L3)
source: she commenced physiotherapy at his wife's clinic in or about September 1996 when she was complaining of back pain extending from T12 level to L3.
the emergence in September 1996 of lumbar pain.
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the abdomen, lower back, lumbar spine or pelvis, unspecified

manifestations.description: constant pain over the back of the neck and left shoulder
persistent neck and shoulder pain with numbness and paraesthesia of the left index and middle fingers
A year later the left index finger had paraesthesia localised to the tip.
there was marked loss of lordosis (inward curve of the spine)
she now had cervical kyphosis (outward curve of the spine)
Dr. Lee found severe limitation on rotation in both directions.
there was still residual numbness of her left index finger which was colder, smaller and more clumsy than her right index finger.
the emergence in September 1996 of lumbar pain
restriction of movement with remissions and relapses requiring courses of physiotherapy

treatments_future: physiotherapy (intermittent courses when aggravated) - judge allowed 15 sessions per annum

losses.description: Pain and suffering and loss of amenity (general damages $300,000).
Loss of overtime earnings (pre-trial and post-trial combined as assessed = $704,674.00).
Loss of full and half pay and earlier increment (26 February to 28 November 1997) $75,760.00.
Physiotherapy (future) allowed at $6,750 per year for 15 sessions, multiplier 10 = $67,500.00.
